reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must accept a level-66 RENAMES whose data-name-2 and data-name-3 are elementary or group items of the same logical record (the one the 66 entries follow), and refuse one whose operands lie in another record, name the same data-name twice, or name a 66, 77, 88 or 01 entry.

edition-consulted.switches: below 2002 RegionClauseCandidates counts the whole scope's candidates (no implicit qualification by the record) and the caller then requires IsWithinRegion; from 2002 only the record's own subtree is searched

reader.edition-search: read RegionClauseCandidates/EntryClauseCandidates and ScreenRenamesOperand; grep Edition|DialectLevel in ResolveRedefinesPass.cs and DataBinder.cs around the RENAMES path; ScreenRenamesOperand and ScreenRenamesWindowOrder have no edition arm
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 an unqualified operand name that also occurs in another record is ambiguous (COBOL1639, §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SR3) where 2023 resolves it within the record; at 85 a 66 operand is found and refused by its level, at 2023 it is not in the record's subtree and is refused as no item of the record
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover legal ranges and an undefined operand; not exercised: same data-name twice, 66/77/88/01 operands, an operand in another record

probes.printed: COBOL2740 R-SAME A THRU A (end of data-name-3 does not follow data-name-2); COBOL2740 R-66 'R1' level 66; COBOL1655 R-77 'W77' not an item of the record; COBOL1655 R-88 'A-ON' not an item of the record; COBOL2740 R-01 'REC' level 1; COBOL1655 R-OTHER 'O2' and R-OTHER2 'O1' not items of the record
probes.expected: each item of SR4 violated in turn is refused

probes.printed: GRP=AB01K / ELEM=-012 / B=-010 / GT=AB01}CDE / QUAL=XYZZ / REC2=PQRS / FR=12YY
probes.expected: group, elementary (inherits signed numeric attributes), group THRU elementary, qualified operand, and a FILE SECTION record are accepted and alias the right storage

probes.printed: --std 85: error COBOL1639 'R-QUAL' RENAMES 'A' does not uniquely identify a data item; --std 2023: runs, QUAL=XYZZ
probes.expected: 1985 requires qualification of a non-unique operand; 2002+ implicit qualification resolves it in the record

reader.notes: Every item of SR4 is refused at 85: other-record, 77 and 88 operands by the record-confinement check (COBOL1655), 66 and 01 operands by ScreenRenamesOperand's level test (COBOL2740), and the same data-name twice by the SR8 window-order check. The diagnostics cite the 2023 clause numbers at --std 85, which names the right rule in another edition but is not wrong-answer.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-230/r4a.cob at --std 85: RENAMES of an item of the other 01 record under the same FD (R-XREC RENAMES FA1 after REC-B; R-XREC2 RENAMES FB1 THRU FA2) refused COBOL1655; THRU an 88 refused COBOL1655 - all as SR4 requires. BUT r4c.cob: '66 R-QQ RENAMES A OF G1 THRU A OF G2.' (two distinct items spelled with the same data-name A, qualified per SR5) compiles and runs at --std 85, printing 'QQ=ABCDEF'. SR4 says data-name-2 and data-name-3 'cannot be the same data-name', and the 1985 glossary defines 'data-name' in a general format as 'a word' (the user-defined word), so the literal reading refuses A OF G1 THRU A OF G2; the reader's requirement reads it as 'the same data item', which SR8 already forbids (the reader's only probe of this clause, A THRU A, is refused by the SR8 window-order check COBOL2740, not by any SR4 check). cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR4 ... the text is in SR4 ('and cannot be the same data-name'); OK  §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR5 ('Data-name-2 and data-name-3 may be qualified'); OK  §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR8; OK  §1985:III.2  (2. DEFINITIONS) the text is in the clause ('represents a word which must not be reference-modified').
refuter.corrected: Reading-dependent: under the word reading (glossary §1985:III.2 'Data-Name') the verdict is UNDER-REJECTS (A OF G1 THRU A OF G2 accepted, ScreenRenamesOperand/ScreenRenamesWindowOrder have no same-word check); under the same-item reading it CONFORMS. The text does not settle which.
